races.name: Racing To School Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Louis Veron
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 5yo in fine recent form (2-21) over similar good ground, trained by Dan Skelton (9 winners from 22 in 14 days) and ridden by Harry Skelton — an organised yard in excellent nick; 13 days since last run, course distance suits.

runners_data.name: Black Dakota
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 7yo with unknown preferred style (U), modest recent form (4th and 5th), ridden by a 5lb claimer; good-ground form is limited and no obvious tactical edge in this shape.

runners_data.name: Colibri Bleu
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 5yo with an awkward recent record (FPP-P3) and only one similar-going run on file; style unknown, which makes placing difficult, and trainer T Ellis is lightly represented (1 winner from 5 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Maskarvel
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-running 5yo who has been placed in five of seven similar-ground runs; Jonathan Burke is a solid pilot and the horse's ability to track the pace closely makes it a danger if Take The Boat weakens.

runners_data.name: McGrath From Clune
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse (true style H) redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is crowded with hold-up types; at OR=82 and aged 10, this is the lowest-rated runner in the field and needs others to blunder for relevance.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse fresh after 289 days off, stepping up from flat/bumper distances; good-ground form is sparse (7/15 similar-going) and the jockey (Paddy Hanlon, 5lb claimer) is inexperienced at this level — intriguing wildcard but plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Usyk
runners_data.note: True hold-up 5yo who needs the pace to be genuine to close late; ridden by a 7lb amateur claimer (Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell) which is a notable disadvantage at a competitive weight, but three of four similar-ground starts produced a placed run.

runners_data.name: Tequila Star
runners_data.note: Flagged as fading in finish — a significant concern in any scenario; a 3yo carrying 151lbs stepping into hurdles with a poor record (8-8-9-8-5 recent), no wins, and limited soft/good-ground form; likely outclassed.

runners_data.name: Angel Of My Dreams
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse (true style H) redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is crowded — in practice will try to find a position off the pace; flagged as fading in finish, which is a serious concern unless the pace is very steady; showed a win last time out (1/08) but softer-ground form is patchy.

runners_data.name: Take The Boat
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner and the race-shaper; 4yo lightly raced (form: 2 run), fresh at 17 days, ridden by Harry Bannister for Georgina Nicholls; without a rival to press, will control tempo and represents the single biggest pace influence in the race.

races.paceDynamic: Take The Boat is the sole confirmed front-runner and, ridden by Harry Bannister, will dictate from the front at a pace likely to be measured rather than brutal — this is a one-horse show up front and there is no rival to press them into a faster-than-comfortable tempo. Louis Veron and Maskarvel will track closely in the prominent positions behind, creating a tight, organised early order, but neither is a true forcing type so the gallop should remain honest rather than searching. With a single pace-setter operating unchallenged, the race is likely to be run at a controlled tempo that sets up a strong finish, favouring hold-up horses who can produce a sustained run from off the pace — Usyk, Penzance, and Angel Of My Dreams are the main beneficiaries of this shape if they can travel well enough into contention. The field holds more hold-up types than can all be placed at the rear cleanly: Angel Of My Dreams and McGrath From Clune are true hold-up horses redistributed into the midfield map position because the rear is congested — in practice, some of these will be forced to race closer than ideal, while those who settle best off the steady pace will be best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Cuts It
scenarios.trigger: If Take The Boat bowls along at a fair but uncontested pace and controls the race from the front throughout
scenarios.body: Take The Boat, unchallenged up front, can dictate the fractions and potentially steal a winning break turning for home; a controlled tempo also means those prominent just behind — Louis Veron and Maskarvel — will always be travelling within themselves and are dangerous late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly slow and hold-up runners get a well-timed run from the back stretch
scenarios.body: A pedestrian tempo compresses the field and allows Usyk or Angel Of My Dreams to produce a late surge that catches the leader flat-footed in the final climb; the amateur claim on Usyk (Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell, 7lb) is a factor but the profile suits if she delivers at the right moment.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Take The Boat weakens after the last and the prominent duo press on
scenarios.body: Louis Veron, with Dan Skelton's yard in fine form (T14: 9/22) and solid recent form (2-21), is ideally placed just behind the leader and can quicken most sharply under Harry Skelton; Maskarvel has consistent placed form and Jonathan Burke can deliver a measured challenge if the gallop has been sustainable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Rank Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses, falls occur, or the leaders badly misjudge the race
scenarios.body: A scrambled finish with no clear leader could bring almost any runner into contention; Penzance, a big-priced hold-up type who has shown ability at better levels (flat form) and is fresh at 289 days, is the each-way wildcard in a messy race.

watchPoints.text: Take The Boat — if Harry Bannister allows even a fractional increase in tempo around the final bend, the entire prominent group (Louis Veron, Maskarvel) will be immediately on the bridle and the leader could be swallowed up; monitor the pace at the third-last.

Usyk and Angel Of My Dreams — both true hold-up types relying on a strong pace that may not materialise; if the gallop is steady, their late runs could be cut short by a compressed field, making them vulnerable to the prominent pair.

Penzance — 289 days off and a switch from flat/bumper to hurdles is a substantial ask; jockey is a 5lb claimer with limited jumps experience, and any jumping hesitancy from a returning, inexperienced horse is a real risk.

Tequila Star — consistent finisher of 8th or worse on recent starts with a fading-in-finish flag; a 3yo in a novice hurdle against older rivals, this runner should be monitored only to confirm it does not become a jumping hazard for others.

McGrath From Clune — at OR=82 and aged 10, the oldest and lowest-rated runner; redistributed to midfield but his natural hold-up style is unlikely to be rewarded in a slow-run race; watch only to see if headgear (tp) produces an early position change.

races.name: Stratford Supporting Racing Staff Week Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Buxted Reel
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner who will lead throughout; Tom Lacey yard is 0/8 in the past 14 days, but the tactical advantage of an uncontested lead on Good ground is substantial — watch for whether he quickens or fades from two out based on his recent 8-of-16 run at Good.

runners_data.name: Dublinofficecallin
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has a single win on Good ground and ran well when last successful over 20f; Ewan Whillans trains from Scotland and 0/14 in 14 days is a concern, but the Good surface removes the soft-ground vulnerability that has blighted most of his recent starts.

runners_data.name: Mayday Games
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse returning from 254 days off with a pull-up and fall on recent form; the fade-in-finish flag compounds concerns about fitness and jumping soundness — a significant lay-off for a horse that has shown little in similar conditions.

runners_data.name: Giddyupadingdong
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has a single win on Good ground and has placed four times in similar conditions; Bradley Harris's 3lb claim helps at the weights and a 23-day turnaround suggests good fitness — his headgear (tongue-tie) is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Estate Planning
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with five consecutive finishes on soft or good-to-soft who has yet to win on this Good surface; 132 days off, zero wins and two places in 15 similar-going runs make this a difficult profile to favour in the current race shape.

runners_data.name: Hellion
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by style, redistributed to midfield on the map solely because the field contains more hold-up types than the rear can accommodate; Donald McCain's yard is 2/25 in 14 days, and his headgear (pads) suggests a management issue — his Good-ground form shows no win from five attempts.

runners_data.name: Papa Oscar
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by running style, redistributed to midfield on the map because of the volume of hold-up runners in this field; his best form came over 16f on Good ground but he has not won in eight attempts at similar conditions — Clare Hobson's stable is 0/4 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Northern Rose
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by style, redistributed to midfield solely because this field holds more rear-runners than the map can place; her profile is striking — 14 runs on Good ground with six places and zero wins, and 241 days off is a significant fitness query despite her consistent placed form at this level.

runners_data.name: Kotgar
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse, redistributed to midfield on the map because of the volume of hold-up runners; his headgear (pads) and 83-day absence are noted, and his form on Good ground (six runs, one place) offers little to recommend him beyond the low OR of 76 giving weight relief.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Spirit
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by style, redistributed to midfield on the map because of the concentration of hold-up types; the fade-in-finish flag and amateur rider (7lb claim) are significant concerns, and his form (0, 8, 10, 9, 13) across conditions including Good suggests limited ability at this level.

runners_data.name: Hopjes
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse, redistributed to midfield because too many hold-up runners are present for all to occupy rear positions; his tongue-tie and 25-day turnaround show active yard management, but his Stratford hurdle form (9th, 11th) and overall record of zero wins from 14 similar-going runs is poor.

runners_data.name: Pink Walls
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse, redistributed to midfield on the map solely due to race shape; his headgear (hood) and recent pull-up/non-finisher form across three runs on Good ground are alarming — three attempts at 16f on Good have produced a non-finish, 12th and non-finish, and this is a difficult profile to support.

races.paceDynamic: Buxted Reel is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate from the outset over 2m½f on Good ground at Stratford, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop without any genuine front-running rival to press him. The field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up horses — Hellion, Papa Oscar, Northern Rose, Kotgar, Cosmic Spirit, Hopjes and Pink Walls are all natural rear-runners who have been redistributed on the map because they cannot all occupy their preferred deep position in a 12-runner field; of these, Papa Oscar and Hellion are most likely to push slightly closer than their natural style suggests, though none will threaten Buxted Reel's lead early. With a solo, uncontested gallop and no pace pressure, Buxted Reel will control the tempo, likely rolling through the middle and final sections at a steady rhythm that compresses the field and reduces the advantage of hold-up horses arriving late. This race shape clearly favours horses able to travel prominently or make a forward move before the final hurdle, as the gallop will be too honest to exploit with a late burst but steady enough to suit a horse seeing out the trip well from a tracking position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solo Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Buxted Reel sets a measured solo gallop and the hold-up pack struggles to close the gap approaching the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: Buxted Reel dictates every yard of the race, and with no rival to apply pressure he conserves energy through the early stages before quickening off his own pace; the hold-up horses face a wall of sustained effort with nowhere to arrive in time. Horses who track from just behind — including Dublinofficecallin if he overcomes his high-mileage soft-ground form — are best positioned to pick up second money.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected over the good ground and Buxted Reel ties up in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: A sustained solo effort at genuine pace will drain Buxted Reel's reserves in the closing stages, opening the door for the more powerful hold-up horses who have been biding their time through the field; Northern Rose's consistent placed form on Good ground and Dublinofficecallin's single win on Good both point to horses who can finish strongly when the pace has been genuine.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed horse such as Hellion or Papa Oscar secures a better position than their natural style suggests and makes a forward move from three out.
scenarios.body: With most of the field committed to the rear, a horse who slips into a prominent tracking role early can time a challenge perfectly off the true pace Buxted Reel sets; Hellion's headgear and recent course form on Good ground make him interesting if William Maggs slots him just off the leader rather than dropping deep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Jumping Errors
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or interference cause a reshuffle, disrupting the controlled race shape and creating an unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: A 12-runner novice hurdle over 2m½f on Good ground carries inherent jumping risk, particularly for Mayday Games (254 days off) and Cosmic Spirit (fade flag, amateur rider) who look vulnerable to errors under pressure; any significant reshuffle would create a lottery but horses with the cleanest recent jumping records and best fitness would benefit.

watchPoints.text: Buxted Reel is the sole pace-maker — if he jumps poorly or deviates at any early hurdle the entire race order collapses and the race becomes a free-for-all among the hold-up pack.

Northern Rose has been off 241 days and Mayday Games 254 days — both are significant lay-off returnees in a novice handicap where fitness levels are untested and jumping errors on Good ground are more likely.

Cosmic Spirit (fade flag, 7lb amateur claim) and Pink Walls (hood, three non-completions on Good) represent the two most vulnerable horses in the field and could cause interference when jumping under pressure in the pack.

The sheer weight of hold-up horses in this field means that if Buxted Reel quickens genuinely from three out, the majority of the field may simply lack the finishing kick to close — horses tracking in the first four lengths of the leader at the top of the straight are statistically far better placed than those arriving from the rear on a tight, turning Stratford circuit.

races.name: Karen Poulter Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Seeyouinmydreams
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner with a confirmed lead style; Good ground record strong (11/15 similar going, 5 wins), has winning form over 16f on Good, Jack Andrews retains the ride and this horse carries 168lbs at OR 120 — the critical variable is whether a front-runner profile holds up under weight at a pace it controls.|

runners_data.name: Nibras Gold
runners_data.note: Prominent traveller with a solid Good-ground profile (13/15, 2W8P) and recent second over 18f on Good; Jonathan Burke takes over and the horse wears headgear (p) suggesting a tendency to need activation — trips over 16-18f on Good suit it well and it should sit ideally placed just off Seeyouinmydreams.|

runners_data.name: In The Air
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with five wins and six places from similar going; Ciaran Gethings partners a horse that has won twice over 16-17f on Good and finished second over 21f on Soft — this shorter trip here on Good looks within range and a T14 stat of 0/9 for trainer Alastair Ralph is the only mild negative flag.|

runners_data.name: Not So Sobers
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse (style=H) who has won back-to-back on Good recently over 16f; 42-day absence (including a fitness flag) is worth noting, David Bass's booking adds confidence, and if the front group obliges with a stronger pace this one has the profile to arrive late — Good ground form is moderate overall (7/15, 2W2P).|

runners_data.name: Whatyouwaitingfor
runners_data.note: A true prominent runner whose natural position cannot be accommodated in this field — mapped to midfield because Seeyouinmydreams, In The Air, and Nibras Gold all want similar ground; Gavin Sheehan will likely have to manage an uncomfortable early compromise, which historically costs horses like this in tight Stratford finishes.|

runners_data.name: Lheur De Gloire
runners_data.note: A natural prominent type redistributed to midfield due to the competitive front-of-race environment; wore a tongue-tie (hg:t) and recent form is encouraging (win 19 days ago over 17f on Good), but Good ground overall record is thin (3/7, 1W1P) and Ben Pauling's T14 of 1/16 suggests the yard is not in peak form.|

runners_data.name: Boom Boom
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a tongue-tie and a form string containing a recent pull-up (P) alongside a previous win over 20f on Good; Robert Dunne rides a horse whose last two public finishes contain a P and a 7, making it difficult to assess true current ability despite a historically decent record on this surface.|

races.paceDynamic: Seeyouinmydreams is the clear front-runner here and, with only one confirmed pace-setter in a seven-runner field, is likely to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop around Stratford's tight 2m1f chase track on Good ground. Nibras Gold and In The Air will push forward to sit close behind, creating a compact prominent group that gives the leader little room to slack off but equally removes any serious pressure that would burn the race out early. The field holds more prominent types than can all get their position — Whatyouwaitingfor and Lheur De Gloire are natural front-runners who will be jostling for space in the early stages and are most likely to be taken back against their will, with Seeyouinmydreams and In The Air better placed to actually secure the ground they want. This race shape — a single leader setting a fair but unspectacular tempo with a cluttered prominent pack — is most likely to produce a winner from the front or close-up positions, with horses who travel fluently in the first half and carry their jump well into the straight having the decisive advantage; genuine hold-up horses face an uphill task if the pace never truly tests the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Seeyouinmydreams sets a fair, uncontested gallop and the prominent bunch stay in a tight group without burning each other out
scenarios.body: Seeyouinmydreams leads throughout at a sustainable pace, and horses who travel prominently and jump fluently into the home straight are best positioned to challenge in the final two fences; In The Air, with strong form on Good and recent course-relevant experience, and Nibras Gold are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Squeeze Suits Bold Traveller
scenarios.trigger: If the early jostling between the prominent group disrupts the redistibuted runners and compresses the field into a single mass through the early stages
scenarios.body: Whatyouwaitingfor and Lheur De Gloire, pushed wide or back against their nature, lose ground they cannot recover on a track where the finish comes quickly; horses already naturally positioned at the front capitalise without burning energy on positional fights

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group sets a stronger-than-expected pace and begin to tire approaching the final fence
scenarios.body: Not So Sobers, freshened by a 42-day break and with back-to-back wins on Good in its recent history, arrives with momentum to pick up a weakening front group; Boom Boom is a wild card from hold-up but its form figures make reliance on it difficult despite a decent winning record on this ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Redistribution Penalties
scenarios.trigger: If the early jostling for position causes jumping errors or interference that eliminates two or more prominent types before halfway
scenarios.body: The race falls open and a horse able to find a clear jumping line regardless of position benefits most; Lheur De Gloire, dropping in from OR 101 and recently winning, could profit if surviving the early scrimmage, while Not So Sobers avoids the carnage entirely from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Watch Whatyouwaitingfor and Lheur De Gloire in the first three fences — both are natural prominent types forced into a compromised position and any early jumping error or interference between them could eliminate them as winning contenders immediately.

Watch the early gallop set by Seeyouinmydreams — if Jack Andrews elects to go very slow, the race will bunch into a sprint finish over the last two fences, which changes the dynamic sharply and could bring Boom Boom or Not So Sobers into contention from the rear.

Not So Sobers has a 42-day break flagged with a fitness concern (17F indicator) — watch in the parade ring and early in the race for any sign of a horse not fully wound up, as David Bass will have to manage fitness reserves if this one is to produce its best in the closing stages.

Boom Boom's form string includes two recent non-completions (P markers) — watch the jumping of this horse throughout as a second jumping failure would confirm that it is best swerved until its jumping is confirmed reliable again.

races.name: Clear Insurance Management Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Machete Beach
runners_data.note: Front-running prominent type who has won twice at similar trips on Good ground in recent form; Gavin Sheehan is a strong booking and Jamie Snowden's T14 strike rate of 3/11 is acceptable; at 5 years old and 17 days fresh, this horse is in form and perfectly placed to dominate an uncontested lead.

runners_data.name: Hooper
runners_data.note: Hold-up style ten-year-old who needs a genuine pace to close into, which this small field and solo front runner is unlikely to generate; tongue tie noted; 37 days since last run for a yard showing 0/3 in 14 days is a concern; Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell's 7lb claim helps weight but adds inexperience to the tactical problem.

runners_data.name: Edelak
runners_data.note: Prominent-style four-year-old who has won and placed on Good going at 16f and has youth and upside on his side; Harry Skelton's presence for Dan Skelton (T14: 12/35) is significant; the hood (p) suggests he needs managing but tracking one leader in a small field suits; 28 days since last run is fine.

races.paceDynamic: Machete Beach is the lone confirmed front runner and will lead from the outset at a sustainable, uncontested tempo over 2m½f on Good ground at Stratford. Edelak, also a prominent-style runner, will track close behind, meaning Machete Beach faces minimal pressure but cannot be allowed to steal a decisive advantage unchallenged. Hooper, a hold-up operator, will be anchored at the rear by Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell and will need the pace to be strong enough to set up a late run, which looks unlikely given just three runners and a single unpressured leader. With a gentle, uncontested gallop virtually guaranteed, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can control the tempo and accelerate from the front — making life exceptionally difficult for a hold-up horse needing a true pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Machete Beach Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Machete Beach dictates a comfortable lead and kicks on turning for home, dictating every fraction unchallenged.
scenarios.body: Machete Beach, armed with a strong recent record at this trip on Good ground (3W4P similar going) and racing fresh off 17 days, controls the race from the front and never comes under serious pressure; Edelak tracks and may be the only danger but carries 2lbs more and has Harry Skelton looking for gaps.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Edelak Challenges and Overpowers
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak tracks Machete Beach closely throughout and outbattles the leader from the last hurdle home.
scenarios.body: Dan Skelton's four-year-old, with Harry Skelton aboard and a T14 strike rate of 12/35, has the class and recent form (1-2 last two outings on Good) to close down a slow leader and get past late; Machete Beach is not an easy target but Edelak is younger, lightly raced, and could have more improvement in the tank.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hooper Delivers Late Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected in the final mile and Hooper finds a clear run to finish powerfully from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Hooper's hold-up style is the hardest to execute in a three-runner race with a single steady pace-setter, but the ten-year-old has a respectable sim-going record (12/15, 1W6P) and retains ability if everything falls right; the amateur rider concedes experience to her rivals, making execution of the hold-up plan even harder.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Flat Finish, Beaten Field
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls home in a tactical stalemate and a messy jump or error shuffles the order late.
scenarios.body: In a race of just three runners on Good ground, a jumping mistake or a moment of hesitation by any horse could dramatically alter positions; Edelak's headgear (p) suggests some controllability issues, and any early drama could compress the finish entirely.

watchPoints.text: Machete Beach — watch whether Gavin Sheehan allows the gallop to die completely; if he crawls, even Edelak can accelerate past him at the last, leaving him vulnerable to a poaching rival.

Hooper — the hold-up style in a three-runner race is a severe structural disadvantage; watch if Jackson-Fennell tries to push forward early, which would represent a significant change of tactics and signal a danger to the front pair.

Edelak — the hood (p) suggests this horse can be keen or needs restraining; if Edelak is allowed to bowl along upsides Machete Beach from the start, the race becomes a true test from an early stage and changes the calculus for Hooper entirely.

Pace sustainability — with only three runners and one confirmed pacer, the sectionals at Stratford's 2m½f will be unusually slow; any horse with a strong jump at the last hurdle could dramatically alter the outcome regardless of position turning for home.

races.name: Happy 80th Birthday David Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tamarind Bay
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse suited by this pace shape; Sean Bowen's booking for Mickey Bowen is a positive yard signal; 77 days off the track is manageable; Good ground form shows 0 wins from 3 placings — places consistently but needs a setup that creates something to aim at late.|

runners_data.name: Harrys Hope
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who should control this race unchallenged; 235 days off the track is the primary concern — Ben Pauling only has 1 run in 14 days suggesting limited prep; strong Good-ground record (3W7P in 15 runs) and won over 2m4f on Good gives distance confidence.|

runners_data.name: Two To Tango
runners_data.note: Natural prominent runner who should hold that position here given the redistribution of rivals; only 17 days since last run and prolific Good-ground form (13/15, 1W11P) makes it the most dependable form reference; headgear (p) suggests consistency management.|

runners_data.name: Mix Of Clover
runners_data.note: A natural prominent type whose true front-running tendency cannot be fully expressed here with Harrys Hope and Two To Tango ahead; mapped to midfield as a consequence of race shape, not natural preference; 12-year-old but has three wins on Good going in recent history including an OR 104 win at 21f; trainer has 0 from 9 in 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Grillon De Monty
runners_data.note: A natural prominent type who is likely forced into a more restrained role by the race shape with confirmed pace-setters ahead; 11-year-old wearing a hood; 30 days since last run is fine; two Good-ground wins at 23f give him a staying profile but he's vulnerable if unable to get his preferred front position.|

races.paceDynamic: Harrys Hope is the confirmed pace-setter and, with only five runners and no genuine challenger for the lead, Sean Bowen on Tamarind Bay will be happy to track from the rear while Charlie Todd on Two To Tango and Ben Jones find their natural rhythm up front. With Mix Of Clover and Grillon De Monty both naturally prominent but unable to secure that position against Two To Tango and Harrys Hope simultaneously, at least one will be forced to settle for a more restrained role than they prefer. The field holds more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Harrys Hope is best-placed to control from the front, with Two To Tango the most likely to press alongside, while Mix Of Clover and Grillon De Monty will find themselves shuffled back from their natural position. At 2m6½f on Good ground with a sustainable, uncontested gallop set by Harrys Hope, this race shape strongly favours a hold-up horse with stamina to pick up the pieces late — Tamarind Bay's profile fits the pace map perfectly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Harrys Hope Controls Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Harrys Hope bowls along at a measured clip and the redistributed prominent types fail to put pressure on early, allowing Ben Jones to dictate terms throughout.
scenarios.body: Harrys Hope sets a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m6½f trip and, with 235 days off the track but strong Good-ground form including three wins in similar conditions, has the fitness question answered by a trainer who gave it just one run in 14 days suggesting a forward showing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Harrys Hope and Two To Tango set a pace that takes its toll on the prominent types in the final mile, leaving Tamarind Bay to produce a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Tamarind Bay, ridden by Sean Bowen for trainer Mickey Bowen with a solid record over similar distances on Good, has the profile to pick off tiring rivals in the closing stages of this stamina test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Mix Of Clover or Grillon De Monty successfully reasserts their natural prominent position and makes it a contested race from the front.
scenarios.body: A messy early scramble for position drains energy from several runners, but the horse that settles best in second or third early — most likely Two To Tango given its consistent Good-ground form (13/15 runs, 1W11P) — stays on most powerfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Veteran Resurfaces With Punch
scenarios.trigger: If Grillon De Monty, at 11 years old but with two wins on Good ground in his history, finds this smaller field suits him and delivers an unexpected staying performance.
scenarios.body: Grillon De Monty's headgear change (hood) combined with the small field and Good going could unlock a competitive performance at OR 102, while his trainer's limited recent activity makes him speculative but not dismissible.

races.name: 19th July Is Ladies Day Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Hiconic
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse at OR 105 with course form at Stratford (2nd and multiple placed at 16f here), Good going confirmed fine, Alex Hales yard in fair 14-day form (2/5), 33 days since last run is acceptable, tongue tie worn — the class horse in the field but will need the sprint finish to set up correctly.|

runners_data.name: Saint Polo
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to race shape congestion; Jennie Candlish yard active (3/24 14-day), 33 days since last run, tongue strap and cheekpieces, has placed at 20f and 24f on Good which suggests stamina if a genuine gallop develops but TS underpins are modest.|

runners_data.name: Backer Bilk
runners_data.note: True hold-up type shown in midfield only because the race shape has no front-runners; a 4-year-old with raw upside, has placed second twice in recent Good-ground hurdles at 16f, 28 days since last run and no headgear concerns — the unexposed profile is a major asset in a sprint finish.|

runners_data.name: Ocean Heights
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse mapped artificially to midfield; David Pipe stable in fair form (4/6), tongue tie and visor worn, best recent form shows two wins from 15 runs on similar going which is a modest strike rate, 20 days since last run keeps him fresh — distance of 18f on Good is within comfort zone.|

runners_data.name: Raffles Nobu
runners_data.note: True hold-up type redistributed to midfield due to race shape; critically only 5 days since last run which raises a bounce risk, headgear includes blinkers, Nick Scholfield conditional jockey angle, has placed third at 20f on Good which confirms stamina — the short turnaround is the key watch point.|

runners_data.name: Stay In The Game
runners_data.note: Listed as non-runner (J:NON-RUNNER) — disregard for race shape analysis; if declared, was an OR 104 hold-up type with course-winning form on Good and would have been a significant player in a sprint finish.|

races.paceDynamic: With every single runner in this six-horse field carrying a hold-up profile, there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse likely to stride into an early lead with purpose — the early stages at Stratford will be tentative, with jockeys eyeing each other and the pace almost certainly crawling until someone is forced to commit. All five runners (Stay In The Game is a non-runner per the data, reducing this to five active participants) are natural hold-up types, meaning the race will compress into a slow-run procession before exploding into a sprint finish from the home straight. All runners are redistributed hold-up types mapped to midfield purely because the race shape has no genuine front-end presence — Hiconic, Saint Polo, Backer Bilk, Ocean Heights, and Raffles Nobu are all true hold-up horses jostling for the same rear-to-midfield positions. A falsely-run sprint finish over the final two flights heavily favours horses with raw tactical speed, a high TS ceiling, and a jockey capable of quick decision-making — in this shape, the horse that can produce the sharpest finishing kick from the lowest point of effort will hold a decisive structural edge over those reliant on genuine stamina.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is suicidally slow and the race degenerates into a cavalry charge from the final hurdle
scenarios.body: With all five horses tracking each other in a tight pack, the race becomes a flat sprint off slow fractions, and the freshest and quickest finisher wins; Backer Bilk and Ocean Heights both show good recent proximity figures on Good and have the tactical zip to fire late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Brave Front Bid Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one jockey loses patience and kicks to make all from halfway, creating a proper test
scenarios.body: A horse that pings to the front from the turn and sustains will catch the field flat-footed from their deep hold-up positions; Hiconic, as the highest-rated hold-up type at OR 105 with proven Stratford form, is most capable of grinding if the pace suddenly escalates.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Class Holds Late
scenarios.trigger: If a moderate gallop gives way to a genuine test of stamina over the final two flights
scenarios.body: In a race where multiple horses tire simultaneously in the sprint, the classiest on official ratings would hold a narrow edge; Hiconic (OR 105) and Backer Bilk (OR 98, improving 4-year-old) each carry enough raw ability to assert when rivals fade.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Drifter Lands Gamble
scenarios.trigger: If one runner is significantly sharpened by a recent run and the race conditions suit a big-priced upset
scenarios.body: Raffles Nobu ran just five days ago (LR:5d) and carries headgear in a race shaped perfectly for a sit-and-sprint; if that bounce concern is absent and the short turnaround proves a sharpener rather than a drain, a fresh-legged upset is conceivable.

watchPoints.text: Raffles Nobu ran just five days ago — monitor market moves to see whether connections expect the short turnaround to sharpen or flatten him, as it is the single biggest swing factor in this race.

With no confirmed front-runner among any of the five runners, watch the early stages closely — any jockey who panics and goes to the front early from a hold-up position could accidentally create a genuine test that catches the true hold-up horses cold.

Backer Bilk is a lightly-raced 4-year-old (only three hurdle runs shown) running at a trip longer than anything in his flat form — if the race develops into a stamina examination rather than a sprint, his inexperience over distance is a vulnerability.

Stay In The Game is listed as a non-runner but had OR 104 and a win at 16f on Good in recent form — confirm non-runner status before race as his inclusion would significantly alter the pace dynamic and class picture.

Conditional jockeys dominate this race (Luke Scott 3lb, Jack Stenhouse 7lb) — in a tactical race with no pace to follow, rider decision-making at the critical moment two out will matter more than in a conventionally-run contest.
